I have successfully updated the URL regex in `rich/highlighter.py` to include the tilde (`~`) character, verified the fix with a reproduction script, and ensured that no test files were modified.

The issue was that URLs containing the tilde character (`~`) were not being fully highlighted by the `ReprHighlighter` in `rich/highlighter.py`. This was due to the URL regular expression lacking the `~` character in its allowed set of characters.

I updated the regular expression in `rich/highlighter.py` to include the `~` character:
- Old regex: `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#]*)"`
- New regex: `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"`

The fix was verified using a reproduction script that confirmed `https://example.org/~user` is now correctly identified as a single URL.
